title: Checked and unchecked exceptions
context: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Checked exceptions extend `Exception` but not `RuntimeException`. The compiler forces callers to catch them or declare them with `throws`. They suit recoverable conditions such as a missing file. Unchecked exceptions extend `RuntimeException` or `Error`. The compiler doesn't force handling. They usually signal programming bugs, such as a null pointer or a bad argument. Error is for JVM-level failures, such as OutOfMemoryError, that application code should not catch.

points.title: Compiler enforcement
points.why: Checked exceptions must be handled or declared. Unchecked ones need no declaration.

points.title: Which to use
points.why: Use checked exceptions for recoverable errors. Use unchecked ones for bugs and invalid arguments.
